title: Animal Bodies
seo_title: Year 1 Science: Animal Bodies Worksheets (Wings, Fins, Legs and Tails)
standard_text: Describe and compare the structure of a variety of common animals (fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals, including pets).
meta_desc: Free Year 1 science worksheets on animal bodies: wings, fins, gills, beaks, shells and whiskers, what each part is for, counting legs and comparing animals. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Each part helps the animal: fins to swim, wings to fly, gills to breathe.
body_html:
How to think about it

Animals have different body parts.

  • Fish have fins and gills. Birds have wings, feathers and a beak.
  • Each body part helps the animal to live.
  • We can compare animals by their body parts.
Example

A fish breathes with?

Under water

Answer: gills

Example

How many legs does a spider have?

More than an insect

Answer: eight

Common mistakes

  • Thinking all animals have four legs.
  • Thinking fish breathe with lungs.
  • Thinking a snake has tiny legs.

faq.q: What body parts do animals have?
faq.a: Many have legs, eyes and a mouth. Fish have fins and gills, birds have wings and beaks, and many mammals have fur, whiskers and tails.

faq.q: Why do animals have different body parts?
faq.a: Each part helps the animal live where it lives: fins to swim, wings to fly, webbed feet to paddle.

faq.q: How many legs do animals have?
faq.a: Birds and humans have 2, many mammals 4, insects 6, spiders 8, and snakes and fish have none.
